Actual Article Body:

JACKSONVILLE, Fla. — Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis, responding to a growing backlash over Flock cameras, has ordered the pole-mounted license plate readers to be removed from all state roads.

The Florida Department of Transportation revoked all permits Monday for license plate readers, most of them owned and operated by Atlanta-based Flock Safety, from the right-of-way of state roads.

State officials said the devices must be removed within 30 days.

The move came less than a week after Mr. DeSantis echoed the concerns of Florida residents who complained the cameras, powered by artificial intelligence, go too far in monitoring the public and are being used in some cases for nefarious reasons by rogue police officers and others.

(Photo by Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

Republican Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said he’s removing automated license plate readers from state roadways, according to a Florida Department of Transportation memo obtained by the Daily Caller.

On Monday, DeSantis ordered all Flock cameras to be removed from the “state highway system,” which includes interstates such as I-10 and I-75, within 30 days. (RELATED: Florida Becomes First State To Ban Tattoos, Vapes For Welfare Program)

The order comes amid growing concerns over the potential misuse of automated license plate readers.

Following the announcement, several sheriff’s departments, including those in Putnam, Liberty and Franklin counties, announced they would end their own license plate reader programs.

The memo further notes that if cameras are not removed from state rights-of-way within 30 days, the state government will remove them itself.
